metadata.note: Ohio River Railroad, Wheeling (Benwood) - Parkersburg - Point Pleasant - Huntington - Kenova, West Virginia, with its Ripley (Millwood - Ripley) and Spencer (Ravenswood - Spencer) branches, and the same lines under the Baltimore and Ohio after July 1901. Split per Rule 4 at the July 1901 change of operator: six ORR features (each staged opening is its own feature, because a feature's geometry cannot grow over time) and five B&O features sharing their geometry. 1912 (outright B&O ownership), 1921 (Wheeling Division) and 1963 (C&O control of the B&O) are not operator changes and are not splits. The line keeps to the West Virginia bank throughout. Research report: research/branches/ohio_river_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-27).
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules of 30 Sept 1951), research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt

metadata.freight_only_audit: Applied at creation, 2026-10-27: not drawn are freight on Wheeling - Huntington after the 1956/1957 end of passenger trains (still the CSX Ohio River Subdivision), Huntington - Kenova freight until lifting in 1965, Spencer Branch freight to the 1964 ICC filing (lifted 1968), Ripley Branch service to 1963, the WV PSC-ordered caboose riding on freights 1957-1971 (unadvertised, no public timetable found), and the West Virginia Short Line (New Martinsville - Clarksburg), rail freight only with buses for passengers in Sept 1951 (OG52 Table 53) and its earlier rail passenger years unresearched.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Applied at creation, 2026-10-27: none - steam from opening.
metadata.not_drawn: West Virginia Short Line, New Martinsville - Clarksburg (59.5 mi), an ORR affiliate that went to the B&O in 1901: opening year, pre-1901 operator and rail passenger end are all unresearched (drawable: NONE in the report). 'Parkersburg Bridge & Terminal': not identified (drawable: NONE). Benwood - Wheeling over the PCC&StL is not a separate feature; it is the north end of orr-wheeling-parkersburg (see that feature's geometry_quality).
not_yet_sourced: bo-ohio-river-huntington-kenova END 1949 is [OPEN]: last confirmed year (WVNC-2 photographs, Dec 1949). The true end is somewhere in the 1950s (WVR, WVNC-2). Read the Kenova times in a clean copy of the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 19, or a later Guide.

bo-spencer-branch END 1951 is [OPEN]: last confirmed year (OG52 Table 21). Later undated evidence: 1953 last steam, a 1954 six-day cut (search summary only), early-1960s undated excursion specials (WVNC-3). A 1953-1963 Official Guide would settle it.
bo-ripley-branch END 1951 is [OPEN]: last confirmed year (OG52 Table 23). WVNC-3's 1963 is probably the end of all service.

Main-line passenger end: 1956 (WVNC-1, Moundsville) vs 1957 (WVNC-2 #72/#73 abolished; CLIO Huntington day trains). Wheeling - Parkersburg is drawn to 1956 and Parkersburg - Huntington to 1957, following the report's drawable spans. A WV PSC discontinuance case c.1956-1960 would settle both, and say what the caboose-riding order required.

orr-wheeling-parkersburg START 1884 rests on two secondary sources plus the heading of an Aug 1884 ORR time table whose station columns are unreadable (SOD84); 1885 is the first year with times (SOD85). Whether trains ran to an intermediate railhead in 1883-84 is unknown.
orr-huntington-kenova START 1894 is the first confirmed year (CA94); ORR trains probably reached Central City in 1893 (unproven).
Guyandotte - Huntington 1888-1892: inferred from PPR88 and WR92S to be over C&O track; not stated outright.
RS&G operator 1892-1901: run as part of the ORR system (WR92A, WR98) but with its own president and reports; whether trains carried RS&G or ORR names is not stated.
Headways and average speeds are estimates throughout (see each segment note and speed_source).

Geometry: the ORR's Kanawha River crossing at Point Pleasant (1887/1888) is drawn on the modern bridge alignment, unchecked; whether Benwood - Moundsville is the ORR's own 1884 track or the parallel B&O main stem was not established.

segments.note: Ohio River Railroad (chartered 1880 as the Parkersburg and Charleston, renamed 1882), Wheeling - Benwood - Moundsville - New Martinsville - Sistersville - St. Marys - Williamstown - Parkersburg (Ann Street station), on the West Virginia bank. North of Benwood ORR trains ran into Wheeling over the PCC&StL (Pennsylvania) (WVNC-1). START 1884: WVNC-1 and CCD say the line was completed Benwood - Parkersburg by 1884, and an ORR passenger time table took effect 24 Aug 1884 (SOD84), though its station columns are unreadable, so how far trains ran that August is not shown; the firmest primary year is 1885, when the May and July time tables (SOD85) show three southbound trains a day leaving Wheeling via Benwood, Moundsville, Clarington, Proctor, New Martinsville, Sardis and Paden's Valley. A piecemeal 1883 opening of the north end is not established. Headway 360 min is an estimate from those three daily trains (four southbound numbers, 1/3/5/7, in the April 1888 table, PPR88T). ENDS 1901 for the change of operator, not for any end of service: the Baltimore and Ohio bought control (announced 11 July 1901, PDP01) and took over operation, moving the general offices and accounts to Baltimore from 1 Aug 1901 (MDL01); service continues on the B&O feature from 1901.
sources: Segment-level: start from WVNC-1, CCD and the Aug 1884 ORR time table heading (SOD84), primary confirmation 1885 (SOD85); end from PDP01/MDL01 (B&O control July 1901). Checked by the research report research/branches/ohio_river_railroad.txt.

segments.note: Ohio River Railroad extension Parkersburg - Washington - Belleville - Ravenswood - Millwood - Letart - Mason City - Clifton - Point Pleasant, 79 mi, built northward from Point Pleasant and laid in 41 working days (PPR87b). START 1887: track was completed in Dec 1886 (PPR86D) and the first through train to Point Pleasant ran on 8 Jan 1887 (PPR87, a Point Pleasant Weekly Register page that LOC dates 6 Jan 1886 but which is evidently the 6 Jan 1887 issue: in Jan 1886 the extension was still only 'proposed', WR86); two passenger trains each way daily Wheeling - Point Pleasant were promised for Feb 1887 (PPR87b). SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded: WVNC-2 and CCD give 1886, which is the construction year, not the first passenger year. Connection with the Kanawha & Ohio at Point Pleasant. Headway 360 min is an estimate (two trains each way promised 1887; the April 1888 time table, PPR88T, carries four southbound numbers). Composition: 38.89 mi OSM old_railway_operator=B&O 'Ohio River Subdivision' (live CSX) to east Huntington; 1.4 mi on B&O-tagged razed/abandoned ways across the Guyandotte River; then 2.2 mi on untagged CSX industrial track along the Huntington riverfront to the B&O station (Heritage Station, hand-pinned at 11th St). segments.note: Ohio River Railroad, Point Pleasant - Henderson - Gallipolis Ferry - Apple Grove - Glenwood - Lesage - Guyandotte - Huntington. Track was in to Guyandotte by Jan 1888 (PPR88); an ORR excursion left Huntington and Guyandotte for Gallipolis Ferry on 1 Apr 1888 (CA88), and the passenger time table effective 8 Apr 1888 runs Wheeling - Point Pleasant - Guyandotte - Huntington with times (PPR88T). START 1888 is therefore exact. GEOMETRY CAVEAT: until about Oct 1892 ORR trains most likely reached Huntington over the C&O main line from Guyandotte and used the C&O passenger depot as a union depot (PPR88; the ORR's own line into Huntington was still being finished in Sept 1892, WR92S) - inferred, not stated outright; see geometry_quality. Headway 360 min is an estimate from the 1888 time table. ENDS 1901 for the change of operator, not for any end of service: the Baltimore and Ohio bought control (announced 11 July 1901, PDP01) and took over operation, moving the general offices and accounts to Baltimore from 1 Aug 1901 (MDL01); service continues on the B&O feature from 1901.

properties.geometry_quality: APPROXIMATED, Rule 2. The Huntington - Kenova line (11.6-12 mi from the Guyandotte River, WR92S/WVR) was lifted in 1965 and is in neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap west of downtown Huntington. Drawn 7.6 mi from the Huntington B&O station: 0.7 mi along untagged railway=abandoned / dismantled OSM ways on the riverfront just west of the station (ways 469068562, 15522089; not proven to be the B&O main line rather than station spurs), then a HAND-PLACED LEG of 6.9 mi from 12th St West to the Kenova town node through four waypoints set by eye on the West Virginia bank between the C&O and the river (a single straight line here cut across the river bend onto the Ohio shore at Burlington, so it was replaced), positions approximate (the B&O's Kenova terminal position is not established). The router's own answer here ran 7.3 mi on the CSX Kanawha Subdivision (the ex-C&O main line) and 0.7 mi on C&O-tagged track; it was rejected so as not to draw B&O trains on the C&O, whose own FFV/George Washington features already cover that track. The real line ran between the C&O and the Ohio River through Central City and Ceredo, the hand-placed leg follows that strip.

segments.note: Ohio River Railroad over the leased Huntington & Big Sandy, Huntington - Central City - Ceredo - Kenova, ~12 mi (WR92S). START 1894 IS THE FIRST CONFIRMED YEAR, not a known opening: the ORR leased the H&BS's 'uncompleted lines' in Sept 1892 (WR92S), the line 'will shortly open for traffic' in Mar 1893 (SADL93) and WVNC-2 says it was 'completed during 1893', but the first positive evidence of trains is a schedule of early June 1894 under which all trains terminate at Kenova 'instead of Central City and Huntington, as heretofore' (CA94) - so trains already reached Central City before June 1894, possibly in 1893 (unproven). SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded: WVNC-2 says the H&BS was 'built extending to Kenova in 1890'; WR92S shows it still uncompleted in Sept 1892. The H&BS never ran trains itself, so no H&BS feature is drawn. Headway 360 min is an estimate (all main-line trains ran through to Kenova from June 1894, CA94). ENDS 1901 for the change of operator, not for any end of service: the Baltimore and Ohio bought control (announced 11 July 1901, PDP01) and took over operation, moving the general offices and accounts to Baltimore from 1 Aug 1901 (MDL01); service continues on the B&O feature from 1901.

segments.note: Ripley & Mill Creek Valley Railroad, Millwood (on the ORR, 45 mi below Parkersburg) - Cottageville - Angerona - Evans - Ripley (Jackson C. H.), 11-13 mi. R. R.' (WDI90), and reported by the ORR general manager as one of 'the two branches of the Ohio River railroad', with passenger earnings for 1897 (WR98) - hence ORR company and colour. START 1888: opened 1 Oct 1888 with trains for the Jackson County fair (WR88O); first regular train 10 Dec 1888 (WR88D). Headway 720 min is an estimate; no 1888-1901 schedule was read. segments.note: Ravenswood, Spencer & Glenville Railway, Ravenswood - Silverton - Sandyville - Leroy - Liverpool - Reedy - Billings - Spencer, 33 mi (WR92A); intended for Glenville and Weston, never got past Spencer. START 1892: opened through to Spencer on 4 Jan 1892 (WSR92); 'Passenger trains are now running regularly from Ravenswood through to Spencer ... Two trains run each way daily' (WDI92). A first section opened in May 1891 (WDI91) but its extent is unreadable, so 1891 is not drawn. OPERATOR CAVEAT: the RS&G was 'built as a portion of the Ohio River railroad system', with the same general officers and ORR-guaranteed bonds (WR92A), and the ORR general manager reported it as one of the ORR's two branches (WR98), so it is drawn in ORR company/colour; but it had its own president (Woodyard) and annual reports, and whether its trains ran in the ORR's or the RS&G's name is not stated. Headway 600 min is an estimate from the two daily trains each way of Jan 1892. ENDS 1901 for the change of operator, not for any end of service: the Baltimore and Ohio bought control (announced 11 July 1901, PDP01) and took over operation, moving the general offices and accounts to Baltimore from 1 Aug 1901 (MDL01); service continues on the B&O feature from 1901.

segments.note: Baltimore and Ohio, ex-Ohio River Railroad, Wheeling - Benwood Jct. - Moundsville - New Martinsville - Sistersville - St. Marys - Williamstown - Parkersburg. The 'Ohio River Division' until 1921, then part of the Wheeling Division (WVNC-1). START 1901: B&O control announced 11 July 1901 (PDP01); general offices and accounts moved to Baltimore from 1 Aug 1901 (MDL01); WVNC-1/WVNC-2/WVE say the B&O began operating the line in 1901. Outright B&O ownership in 1912 and the 1921 division merger did not change who ran the trains and are not splits. In Sept 1951 through trains ran Pittsburgh - Wheeling - Parkersburg - Huntington - Kenova with times at every station (OG52 Table 19), plus a mixed train at Williamstown; Wheeling - Kenova trains #72/#73 are listed at Wheeling in 1942 and #73 is photographed at Williamstown in 1953 (WVNC-1). END 1956 is the earlier of two bracketing figures: WVNC-1 says passenger service 'ceased on the route in 1956' (at Moundsville), while WVNC-2 says #72/#73 were 'abolished in 1957' and CLIO says Huntington's day trains ended in 1957. The 1956 figure may be a station closure rather than the end of trains along the line; not established, so 1957 is withheld here. After the trains ended the WV PSC made the B&O carry riders in freight cabooses until 1971 (WVNC-1); that unadvertised arrangement is not drawn. Freight continues as the CSX Ohio River Subdivision. Headway 360 min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start from PDP01, MDL01, WVNC-1, WVNC-2 (1901); 1951 service from OG52 Table 19 (times present); end 1956 from WVNC-1, conflicting with 1957 in WVNC-2/CLIO (recorded). Checked by the research report research/branches/ohio_river_railroad.txt.

properties.geometry_quality: Same geometry as the two ORR features orr-parkersburg-point-pleasant and orr-point-pleasant-huntington, joined at Point Pleasant: Traced 78.75 mi against 79 mi documented (PPR87b: 'seventy-nine miles of track on the O. R. Railroad extension'). 100% on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O, name 'Ohio River Subdivision' (live CSX). No straight-line legs. Per-station check against the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 19 mileposts (Parkersburg = 161.0): Ravenswood 195.8 drawn vs 195.6, Millwood 207.1 vs 206.6, Letart 211.8 vs 211.6, New Haven 220.6 vs 220.4, Hartford 222.0 vs 222.1, Mason City 225.0 vs 224.9, Clifton 226.5 vs 226.6. The line stays on the West Virginia bank throughout; the K&M/NYC and C&O ex-Hocking Valley lines across the river were not used. Ends at the Point Pleasant waypoint (within 0.3 km). The drawn crossing of the Kanawha River into Point Pleasant is the modern bridge alignment; the date and site of the ORR's original Kanawha crossing were not checked. No realignment is known; not checked against a period map. || Traced 42.51 mi Point Pleasant - Huntington B&O station, against ~45 mi (rough) in the research report; per-station check against the Feb 1952 Guide Table 19 mileposts: Henderson 240.9 drawn vs 241.2, Gallipolis Ferry 246.6 vs 245.5, Apple Grove 254.4 vs 254.8, Lesage 271.7 vs 270.0, Guyandotte 278.7 vs 278.5. Composition: 38.89 mi OSM old_railway_operator=B&O 'Ohio River Subdivision' (live CSX) to east Huntington; 1.4 mi on B&O-tagged razed/abandoned ways across the Guyandotte River; then 2.2 mi on untagged CSX industrial track along the Huntington riverfront to the B&O station (Heritage Station, hand-pinned at 11th St). That riverfront track is probably the surviving end of the B&O line but carries no historic tag, and the ex-C&O Huntington shop tracks lie alongside; it could sit on C&O-owned track for up to ~1 mi. No straight-line legs. By 1901 the ORR's own Guyandotte - Huntington line (1892) was in use, so the C&O caveat on the ORR-era feature does not apply. Total 121.3 mi Parkersburg - Huntington station, vs ~117.5 mi Parkersburg - Guyandotte from the 1951 Guide mileposts plus ~3 mi to the station.

segments.note: Baltimore and Ohio, ex-Ohio River Railroad, Parkersburg - Ravenswood - Millwood - Mason City - Point Pleasant - Gallipolis Ferry - Guyandotte - Huntington. START 1901: B&O control July 1901 (PDP01, MDL01; WVNC-2 'In 1901, Parkersburg emerged as a complete B&O city when the road took control'). In Sept 1951 OG52 Table 19 prints times all the way from Parkersburg through Ravenswood, Millwood, Letart, Mason City, Gallipolis Ferry and Lesage to Guyandotte. END 1957 (approx.): trains #72/#73 (their meet at Letart is pictured in 1955) 'remained in effect until the trains were abolished in 1957 due to declining ridership' (WVNC-2), and at Huntington 'nighttime trains stopped running in 1953, and all daytime passenger trains were halted in 1957' (CLIO). Two independent secondary sources agree; no exact date or discontinuance order was found. Freight continues as the CSX Ohio River Subdivision. Headway 360 min is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: APPROXIMATED, Rule 2. The Huntington - Kenova line (11.6-12 mi from the Guyandotte River, WR92S/WVR) was lifted in 1965 and is in neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap west of downtown Huntington. Drawn 7.6 mi from the Huntington B&O station: 0.7 mi along untagged railway=abandoned / dismantled OSM ways on the riverfront just west of the station (ways 469068562, 15522089; not proven to be the B&O main line rather than station spurs), then a HAND-PLACED LEG of 6.9 mi from 12th St West to the Kenova town node through four waypoints set by eye on the West Virginia bank between the C&O and the river (a single straight line here cut across the river bend onto the Ohio shore at Burlington, so it was replaced), positions approximate (the B&O's Kenova terminal position is not established). The router's own answer here ran 7.3 mi on the CSX Kanawha Subdivision (the ex-C&O main line) and 0.7 mi on C&O-tagged track; it was rejected so as not to draw B&O trains on the C&O, whose own FFV/George Washington features already cover that track. The real line ran between the C&O and the Ohio River through Central City and Ceredo, the hand-placed leg follows that strip.

segments.note: Baltimore and Ohio, ex-Ohio River Railroad (leased Huntington & Big Sandy), Huntington - Central City - Ceredo - Kenova. START 1901 with the rest of the ORR (CA01 lists the H&BS among the lines that went to the B&O). END 1949 IS [OPEN]: the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. The last train seen bound for Kenova is #81, pictured departing Mason for Kenova in 1947 and again in a Dec 1949 scene (WVNC-2). The Feb 1952 Official Guide's Table 19 names Kenova in its title, but the Kenova times are lost in the OCR, so 1951 is not confirmed. 'Some time in the 1950's' B&O trains stopped serving Kenova (WVR); WVNC-2 says 'by the end of the 1950s'. No source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence (move to 1951 only if a Kenova time is read in OG52 Table 19). The track was lifted in 1965. Headway 360 min is an estimate.

segments.note: Baltimore and Ohio Spencer Branch (ex-Ravenswood, Spencer & Glenville), Ravenswood - Spencer, 33.1 mi. START 1901: the RS&G went to the B&O with the ORR in July 1901 (CA01); WVNC-3's 1912 is the formal acquisition and not a change of operator. In WWII 'daily trains #67 and #68 which as common procedure were mixed' (WVNC-3). END 1951 IS [OPEN]: the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Passenger service is confirmed in Sept 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 21, 'Ravenswood and Spencer', with times (leave Ravenswood 13:10, arrive Spencer 15:25). Later undated mentions: renumbering to #457/#458 in the 1950s, last steam 16 Dec 1953, a 1954 cut to six days a week (from a search summary of a local obituary page, HUR, not read directly), and three undated early-1960s 'special excursions as final passenger runs' (WVNC-3). No source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The 1964 ICC abandonment filing and 1968 lifting are not passenger ends. Headway 1440 min: one round trip a day in 1951 (estimate for other years).

Composition: 100% OpenHistoricalMap railway ways, 4.9 mi named 'Ripley and Mill Creek Valley Railroad' and 6.92 mi untagged OHM ways continuing it (OHM ways 201444819, 201444906, 201333031 etc.). segments.note: Baltimore and Ohio Ripley Branch (ex-Ripley & Mill Creek Valley), Millwood - Ripley, ~13 mi. START 1901: the R&MCV went to the B&O with the ORR in July 1901 (CA01); WVNC-3's 1912 is the formal absorption. END 1951 IS [OPEN]: the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Passenger service is confirmed in Sept 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 23, 'Millwood and Ripley', Nos. 961/962, with times (leave Millwood 9:00 a.m., Ripley about 9:40, back at Millwood 11:00 a.m.). WVNC-3's 'Service ended on the Ripley line in 1963' probably means all service and is not taken as the passenger end. One crew worked both the Ripley and Spencer branches in the 1950s (WVNC-3). Possibly a mixed train in the 1950s (not established). No source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 1440 min: one round trip a day in 1951 (estimate for other years).
